observations.text: SP, at first exposure to VOR and TACAN course intercepts, could not determine the intercept heading and the lead point without IP direction, with the result that deviation from the assigned radial reached 12 degrees before the correction was directed. Inbound and outbound tracking was established only after the IP took over part of the problem. Performance is at the desired standard for the Training Section but marginal, since direction was required on every intercept; independent computation of the intercept angle is expected to improve over the next sorties.

SP applied the standardized course intercept procedure of AFMAN 11-202 Vol 3 and completed VOR and TACAN intercepts inbound and outbound with the IP's verbal indications only, without the IP directing or executing any part of the problem. Deviation from the assigned radial remained at 8 degrees and was corrected after the prompt. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP computed the intercept angle and the appropriate lead independently, requiring no verbal indications from the IP. Small errors in the roll-out point produced deviations of 7 degrees from the assigned radial, which SP recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied the standardized procedure accurately and rapidly on VOR, TACAN and GPS (OBS mode) intercepts, both inbound and outbound. Lead was selected correctly for the closure angle and deviation from the assigned radial did not exceed 4 degrees at any point, including the intercept commenced immediately after station passage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP solved the course intercept problem flawlessly on every radial assigned, selecting the lead point without hesitation and holding the Basic A/C Control criteria throughout. Deviation from the assigned radial remained within 2 degrees inbound and outbound, including immediately after station passage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect method of deriving the intercept angle from the CDI displacement and the bearing pointer, did not apply the standardized course intercept procedure and turned toward the assigned radial without an intercept heading. The resulting deviation exceeded 15 degrees and the IP had to direct the intercept heading and execute part of the outbound tracking. Review of the intercept geometry of AFMAN 11-202 Vol 3 is required.

SP, due to mode confusion over the selected avionics mode and what it was protecting, set the OBS to the reciprocal of the assigned course and flew an intercept opposite to the one required. The error was not detected and the IP had to reset the course and direct the recovery to the radial, after a deviation of 20 degrees. Verification of the selected course against the clearance is required before commencing the intercept.

SP determined the intercept heading correctly but delayed the turn at the lead point, and the intercepts were completed after the IP's verbal indications on two occasions. Maximum deviation from the assigned radial was 8 degrees, recognized and corrected with delay. Performance meets the desired standard for the Training Section but is marginal at its limit; earlier recognition of the closure rate is expected to improve.

SP applied the appropriate lead on VOR and TACAN intercepts without verbal indications from the IP, and inbound and outbound tracking was established on each assigned radial. Small errors in bank selection at roll-out produced deviations of 6 degrees, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP solved the intercept problem accurately and rapidly, selecting the intercept angle and the lead point according to the standardized procedure and without IP's intervention. Deviation from the assigned radial did not exceed 4 degrees inbound or outbound, and the intercept commenced immediately after station passage was established without overshoot. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP handled VOR, TACAN and GPS (OBS mode) intercepts with a fluency expected at a far more advanced stage, computing the lead point for each closure angle without hesitation. Deviation from the assigned radial remained within 2 degrees throughout, including immediately after station passage, and the Basic A/C Control criteria were held with negligible excursions. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect application of the intercept geometry, selected an intercept angle smaller than the displacement required and did not use the appropriate lead at roll-out. SP could not re-establish the assigned radial without assistance and the IP directed the intercept heading, with a maximum deviation of 14 degrees. Practice of the standardized intercept procedure of AFMAN 11-202 Vol 3 is required.

SP, due to an error that went undetected because the cross-check was not re-established after station passage, continued outbound on the previous radial without recognizing the reversal of the CDI. The deviation grew beyond 15 degrees and the IP had to take over the tracking to return the A/C to the assigned course. Re-establishing the navigation cross-check immediately after station passage is required.

SP, due to a late turn onto the intercept heading, did not commence the intercept with the appropriate lead and remained displaced through the roll-out. The intercept was completed only after the IP's verbal indications, with a maximum deviation of 8 degrees from the assigned radial, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to poor workload distribution, with navigation, communication and aircraft control attempted simultaneously, did not update the intercept solution when a new radial was assigned. The correction was applied only after the IP's verbal indications and deviation from the assigned radial reached 8 degrees before it was recognized. Shedding the secondary task before recomputing the intercept is required.

SP executed VOR and TACAN course intercepts within the desired standards, computing the intercept angle without IP's intervention. However, the lead point was twice taken late and the resulting deviations of 7 degrees were recognized and corrected in a timely manner. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in lead selection and in outbound tracking is expected to improve.

SP applied the standardized course intercept procedure accurately and rapidly on every radial assigned, inbound and outbound, without IP's intervention. Lead was appropriate for the closure angle and deviation did not exceed 4 degrees, including the intercept commenced immediately after station passage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP solved the intercept problem flawlessly on VOR, TACAN and GPS (OBS mode), selecting the intercept angle and the lead point without hesitation while maintaining the Basic A/C Control criteria. Deviations from the assigned radial were negligible, remaining within 2 degrees inbound and outbound. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to insufficient knowledge of the intercept geometry, did not convert the radial displacement into an intercept heading and turned to a heading parallel to the assigned course. The IP had to direct the intercept heading and execute the roll-out onto the radial, after a deviation of 16 degrees. Study of the course intercept procedure of AFMAN 11-202 Vol 3 is required before the next instrument sortie.

SP, due to over-reliance on automation that was not fully understood, accepted the GPS (OBS mode) course indication without an independent check against the TACAN radial and flew an intercept to a course that had not been assigned. The error was not recognized and the IP directed the reselection and executed part of the tracking, with the A/C displaced more than 12 degrees from the assigned radial. An independent cross-check of the selected course against the clearance is required.

SP, due to the selection of an intercept angle excessive for the displacement present, did not use the appropriate lead and overshot the assigned radial on two intercepts. Both were re-established only after the IP's verbal indications, with a maximum deviation of 8 degrees, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to an interrupted instrument cross-check while attention remained on the navigation display, did not monitor the closure to the assigned radial and did not commence the turn at the lead point. The IP's verbal indication was required on each intercept and deviation reached 8 degrees before the correction was applied. Timely recognition of the closure rate is expected to improve with a re-established scan.

SP, due to a late roll-out from the intercept turn, did not stabilize the inbound tracking on the first attempt and applied a correction larger than the displacement required. Deviation from the assigned radial reached 6 degrees, recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established outbound, delayed the recomputation of the intercept after a new radial was assigned. The lead point was taken late and deviation reached 7 degrees, which SP recognized and corrected without IP's intervention. Protecting the navigation cross-check during transmissions is expected to improve.

SP executed VOR, TACAN and GPS (OBS mode) course intercepts accurately and rapidly, applying the appropriate lead without IP's intervention, and tracking was established timely inbound and outbound. Performance was within the desired standards, with deviation reaching 5 degrees on the intercept commenced immediately after station passage. Marginal for the Training Section - tighter control of the roll-out point after station passage is expected to improve.

SP applied the standardized intercept procedure with a precision above the level required at this stage, anticipating the lead point for each closure angle and re-establishing the cross-check immediately after station passage. Radial deviations were negligible, not exceeding 2 degrees on any intercept, inbound or outbound. Above end of block MIF achieved.
